title: Countries
summary: The shortest list in the application, and the one the others lean on.
text:
Countries

The shortest list in the application, and the one the others lean on.

 Field | |
 
 Country | The name of the country. It is the key: it is what jobs and customers refer to. |
 Currency | The currency of that country. Required. |

The currency is what makes the salary range of a job mean something: a minimum of 20.000 is not
the same number in two countries, and the country is what says which.

 Before deleting one

A country used by a job or by a customer cannot be deleted.

title: Customers
summary: Who buys from the company, and what they ordered.
keywords: What a customer is made of
text:
Customers

Who buys from the company, and what they ordered.

 What a customer is made of

 Field | |
 
 Customer Id | The number that identifies the customer. |
 Customer Name | Required. |
 Contact Firstname, Contact Lastname | The person to talk to. |
 Phone no, City, State/Province | Where and how to reach them. |

 Orders

Open a customer and the tab underneath holds their orders:

 Field | |
 
 PO number | The order number. It is the key. |
 Order status | Where the order stands. Required. |
 Order date | When it was placed. Required. |
 Ship date, Date needed | When it left, and when it was wanted. |
 Qty ordered, Total value, Discount | How much, for how much, less how much. |
 Item type | What kind of goods. |
 Paid | Whether it was paid. |

Orders are saved together with the customer they belong to.

 Exporting

The toolbar carries Download in CSV and Download in Excel: what comes out is the customers
the list is showing, filters included.

title: Departments
summary: The departments of the company. They are a tree: a department may have a parent department, which is how a division contains its offices.
keywords: What a department is made of
text:
Departments

The departments of the company. They are a tree: a department may have a parent department,
which is how a division contains its offices.

 What a department is made of

 Field | |
 
 Dept no | The code, three characters. It is the key, and it is what the other screens refer to. |
 Department | The name. Required. |
 Budget | The budget of the department. |
 Location | Where it is. |
 Phone no | The switchboard number. |
 Head department | The department this one belongs to, if any. Leave it empty for a department at the top. |
 Manager | The employee who runs it. |

 Before deleting one

A department with employees in it, or with another department under it, cannot be deleted. Move
those first.

title: Employees
summary: The people of the company: what they are paid, when they were hired, which department they belong to and what job they hold.
keywords: What an employee is made of
text:
Employees

The people of the company: what they are paid, when they were hired, which department they belong
to and what job they hold.

 What an employee is made of

 Field | |
 
 First name, Last name | Required. The full name shown by other screens is built from them. |
 Phone ext | The internal extension, four characters. |
 Hire date | The day the employee was hired. Required. |
 Salary | The current salary. Required - and see the salary history below, which is where its changes are kept. |
 Department | One of the departments. Required. |
 Job | One of the jobs. Required. |

A job carries a minimum and a maximum salary for the country it belongs to, so a salary and a job
that disagree are a thing worth checking before saving.

 Salary history

Open an employee and the tab underneath holds the changes to that salary, one row each:

 Field | |
 
 Change date | When the change was applied. Part of the key: two changes to the same employee on the same date by the same person are the same row. |
 Updater id | Who applied it. |
 Old salary, New salary, Percent change | What it was, what it became, by how much. |

The history is saved together with the employee it belongs to.

 Exporting

The toolbar offers Download in TXT besides the usual buttons: it takes away the employees the
list is showing, filters included.

title: KEmployee
summary: KEmployee is a demo application of the KittoX framework built on the employee database that ships with Firebird - the one with departments, jobs, projects and a sales history. It is a company seen from its personnel office: who works where, on what, for how much, and who buys from it.
text:
KEmployee

KEmployee is a demo application of the KittoX framework built on the employee database that
ships with Firebird - the one with departments, jobs, projects and a sales history. It is a
company seen from its personnel office: who works where, on what, for how much, and who buys from
it.

 The menu

 Folder | What is inside |
 
 Tables | The lists the rest of the application chooses from: countries, jobs, departments. |
 Business | The day to day: customers with their orders, employees with their salary history, and projects. |
 Maintenance | Close session, which ends your session. |

 Where to start

Open Employees: it is the screen with the most in it, and it shows in one place what every
other screen does separately - a search panel, a form, and a tab underneath with the records that
belong to the one you are looking at. Lists and forms explains those once.

 A word about the data

It is demo data: salaries, orders and dates are the ones Firebird ships for teaching, not a real
company. Nothing you change here reaches anything but your own copy of the database.

title: Jobs
summary: The jobs an employee can hold. A job is not only a title: it carries the salary range it is paid within, and that range is per country, because the same job is not paid the same everywhere.
keywords: What a job is made of
Why the key is made of three fields
text:
Jobs

The jobs an employee can hold. A job is not only a title: it carries the salary range it is paid
within, and that range is per country, because the same job is not paid the same everywhere.

 What a job is made of

 Field | |
 
 Job code | The code, up to five characters. |
 Job grade | The grade. Part of the key together with the code and the country: the same code at two grades is two jobs. |
 Job country | One of the countries. Part of the key. |
 Job title | The name of the job. Required. |
 Min salary, Max salary | The range this job is paid within, in the currency of its country. Required. |
 Job requirement | What the job asks for, as long a text as you need. |
 Language req | The language it requires. |

 Why the key is made of three fields

A job is the same job only when code, grade and country are the same. That is what lets the
same title exist at two grades, and in two countries with two different salary ranges, without
the records getting in each other's way.

 Before deleting one

A job someone holds cannot be deleted: look at the employees first.

title: Lists and forms
summary: Every screen of KEmployee is a list, and the same handful of gestures works on all of them.
text:
Lists and forms

Every screen of KEmployee is a list, and the same handful of gestures works on all of them.

 The search panel

Above the rows, a panel narrows what the list shows: Search Employees, Search Customers,
 Search Projects, Search Departments, Search Jobs, each with the filters that screen
offers. Filters add up, and emptying one puts back the rows it was hiding.

 The toolbar

 New, Edit, View, Delete, Refresh - add a record, change it, read it without
the risk of changing it, remove it after a confirmation, read the rows again.

A record other records depend on cannot be deleted: a department with employees, a job someone
holds, a country a job belongs to. The application says what is holding it rather than letting the
database refuse with a message nobody can read.

 Sorting, paging, exporting

Click a column heading to sort by it, click again to reverse. Long lists are read a page at a
time. Where a screen offers it, the toolbar carries Download in CSV, Download in Excel or
 Download in TXT, and what comes out is what the list is showing - filters included.

 Tabs under a form

Some records own others: an employee owns a salary history, a customer owns orders. Those appear
in a tab under the form of the record they belong to, with a toolbar of their own, and they
are saved together with it.

title: Projects
summary: Field | |    Proj id | The code, up to five characters. It is the key. |  Proj name | The name. Required. |  Product | The product the project belongs to. |  Team Leader | The employee who leads it. |  Proj desc | The description, as long as you need. |
keywords: What a project is made of
Who works on it, and on whose budget
text:
Projects

What the company is working on.

 What a project is made of

 Field | |
 
 Proj id | The code, up to five characters. It is the key. |
 Proj name | The name. Required. |
 Product | The product the project belongs to. |
 Team Leader | The employee who leads it. |
 Proj desc | The description, as long as you need. |

 Who works on it, and on whose budget

Two things connect a project to the rest of the company, and they are worth knowing even though
each is a table of its own:

 Employee projects says which employees work on which projects. The same employee may be on
 several, and a project has several people on it.
 Project department budgets says, for a fiscal year, how much a department put into a
 project and with how many people: the key is the three of them together - year, department,
 project - which is what lets two departments fund the same project in the same year.

 Before deleting one

A project with people on it, or with a budget recorded against it, cannot be deleted.
